name: נַעֲרָה
summary: One of the two wives of Ashhur the father of Tekoa, of Judah, and mother of Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni and Haahashtari (1Ch 4:5–6). The name is the noun נַעֲרָה “girl, young woman” itself, the word used of Rebekah, Ruth and Esther (Gen 24:16; Rut 2:5; Est 2:7); scripture does not explain why she was called so.

evidence.note: “Ashhur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and נַעֲרָה.”
“Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni and Haahashtari; these were the sons of Naarah.”
The common noun: “the נַעֲרָה was very good of appearance.”

note: BDB's key n.ei.ah is left off: it counts 14 tokens, most of them the noun נַעֲרָה “girl” by spelling (Deu 22:23, 28; 1Ki 1:2–3; Est 2:3, 12), and the person is only 1Ch 4:5–6. The place Naarah (Jos 16:7, n.ei.ag) is a different bearer and is not a person. The cognates are those of the masculine נַעַר; none of the feminine has been followed to its own dictionary.
